course_name_original: Cálculo, diseño y ensayo de máquinas (596)
course_name_en: Calculation, Design and Testing of Machines
prerequisites: Science of materials (492): Knowledge of stress-strain diagrams: proportionality limit, elastic limit, yield stress, ultimate stress, and Young's modulus.
Theory of mechanisms (493): Equilibrium and free-body diagrams in mechanisms. Kinematics of pure rolling. Basic concepts of gears: nomenclature, conjugate action, and involute profile.
Strength of materials (495): Mohr's circles. Stresses in resistant elements subjected to axial, shear, bending, and torsional forces.

learning_outcomes.text: Understand the fundamentals of Mechanical Machine Element Design.
Clearly identify the forces that machine elements withstand in different operating scenarios.
Know the different failure criteria for machine elements.
Identify stresses, material, and working scenario to apply the most appropriate failure criterion for each circumstance.

syllabus_topics: Introduction and development of a design process.
Fundamentals of basic concepts: stresses, stiffness, deformation, statistical considerations, materials and their properties.
Preventive failure and/or fracture criteria, in constant and variable load scenarios.
Design of mechanical transmissions: transmission shafts/axles.
Gear calculation: general description, spur gears, helical gears, bevel gears, and worm gears.
Design and calculation of mechanical transmissions with flexible elements: Transmission belts, chain drives, cables, flexible shafts.
Design, calculation, and testing of brakes and clutches.
Calculation of bolted joints.
Calculation of welded joints.
Calculation of springs.
Design and calculation of keys and couplings.

Tema 1: Introduction - Design in mechanical engineering. Phases and interactions of the design process. Design tools and resources. Professional responsibilities of the design engineer. Standards and codes. Safety factor. Reliability. Material selection. Equilibrium and free-body diagrams. Stresses and strains. Cartesian components of stress. Mohr's circles. Stress concentration.

Tema 2. Failure under static loads - Mechanical failure. Theories of failure under static load for ductile materials: maximum shear stress theory, distortion energy theory, Mohr-Coulomb theory. Theories of failure under static load for brittle materials: maximum normal stress theory, modifications to Mohr's theory.

Tema 3. Failure under dynamic loads - Fatigue in metals. Wöhler curve. Fatigue strength and fatigue limit. Modifying factors of the fatigue limit. Stress concentration and notch sensitivity. Characterization of fluctuating stresses. Fatigue failure criteria. Cumulative fatigue damage.
Tema 4. Transmission shafts - Axles and transmission shafts. Shaft configuration. Design of transmission shafts for bending and torsion. Keys and couplings.

Tema 5. Joints - Bolted joints. Thread standards and definitions. Power screws. Calculation of bolted joints working under tension. Calculation of bolted joints under shear. Welded joints. Butt and fillet welds. Stresses in welded joints subjected to torsion and bending. Strength of welded joints.
Tema 6. Springs - Stresses in helical springs. Compression springs. Extension springs. Helical torsion springs. Belleville springs.

Tema 7. Gears - Nomenclature. Types of gears. Conjugate action. Involute profile. Contact ratio. Interference. Gear trains. Force analysis in gears. Spur gears. Helical gears. Bevel gears. Worm screws. Lewis equation.

Tema 8. Clutches and brakes - Static analysis of clutches and brakes. Internal expanding drum clutches and brakes. External contracting clutches and brakes. Band clutches and brakes. Axial friction contact clutches. Disc brakes. Conical clutches and brakes.
Tema 9. Flexible transmissions - Flat belts, round belts, V-belts, timing belts. Chains. Cables. Flexible shafts.

A minimum attendance of 90% is required in laboratory and computer practicals for the "Reports and practice reports" evaluation system to be computed. Fraudulent completion of an evaluation test will result in a 0 for that test and a numerical grade of 0 for the subject in that examination call.
